question: A 58-year-old male presents with hoarseness of two months' duration. Laryngoscopy shows the left vocal cord fixed in the paramedian position. Which feature of the anatomy of the left recurrent laryngeal nerve best explains why left-sided vocal cord palsy is more common than right-sided?

answers.text: The left RLN hooks around the aortic arch, making it vulnerable to mediastinal and apical lung lesions.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The left RLN has a longer intrathoracic course, looping under the aortic arch, so mediastinal lymph nodes, aortic aneurysm, and left apical lung carcinoma are important causes of left-sided palsy.

answers.text: The left RLN crosses the subclavian artery, placing it at risk during thyroid surgery.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. It is the right RLN that hooks around the right subclavian artery. The left RLN has its vulnerable turn around the aortic arch.

answers.text: The left RLN enters the larynx from the posterior aspect of the cricothyroid joint, making it susceptible to thyroid cancer.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Partially relevant but not the reason for left-sided predominance. Both RLNs enter near the cricothyroid joint; the key difference is the longer left intrathoracic course.

answers.text: The left RLN runs in the tracheo-oesophageal groove on the anterior surface of the oesophagus, making it susceptible to oesophageal carcinoma.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Both RLNs run in the tracheo-oesophageal groove in the neck. The characteristic vulnerability of the left RLN to intrathoracic pathology is due to its loop around the aortic arch, not oesophageal proximity alone.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the course of the left versus right RLN. The left loops around the aortic arch intrathoracically; this longer mediastinal course accounts for the higher incidence of left-sided vocal cord palsy from thoracic pathology.
Well done. The long intrathoracic course of the left RLN (looping under the aortic arch) is the anatomical basis for its greater susceptibility — always consider thoracic causes for left VCP.
